content.thinking:
Looking at the timeline now: the monthly-spend feature flag was switched on by an admin at 22:24:18Z, and that's when the ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py started hitting account page requests. I'm also tracking how the mitigation went: the flag was reverted off at 22:29:35, but the incident stayed at the same level, so I'm working through why that happened and what the flag being put back on at 22:

The logs show that errors kept appearing at 22:31, 22:34 and 22:40 even though the provider had already reported the flag as off, so the revert may not have reached every replica. The highest error rate was on one replica at 22:31, which suggests cached flag values could be the reason the mitigation didn't help.

Now I'm checking which deploys and changes can be ruled out, since the change record shows only the three flag changes in the window and every replica is on one revision.

I'm now tracing the causal chain: account page requests failed, the failing requests raised a ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py, and those requests were the ones that evaluated the monthly-spend feature flag as on, which lines up with the admin switching it on. Deploys are ruled out for this window, since every replica is on one revision.

I'm working out the causal chain now: the failing requests hit a division in the spend summary, and that division can produce zero when a shopper has no purchases this month, which is why the flag path fails for them.

I'm weighing whether a check before the flag switch-on would have caught this, since the division was already in the code behind the flag and no test seemed to cover a shopper with past purchases but none this month. The fault-specific test that this incident's fix covers doesn't address the missing pre-enable check, so that needs its own item. I'm also looking at the second contributing factor, the flag being switched on for all traffic at once.

I'm checking the remaining contributing factors now: there was no guard that would have turned the flag back off when account page errors rose after the switch-on. I'm not counting that one, since the revert at P2 didn't end the harm, so I'm dropping it. I'm also noting that nobody was paged, so there's no on-call incident linked to this.

Now I'm noting that nobody was paged for this incident, so the alert went without a human response, and I'm weighing whether that gap belongs among the contributing factors. I'm also checking why the alert fired later than its evaluation window accounts for, since the record doesn't explain roughly three minutes of that delay.

I'm checking whether the flag revert actually reached every evaluation, since errors kept showing up on flag-on evaluations after the revert was logged. If the off state didn't propagate, that would explain why the mitigation didn't stop the harm, and it's a condition worth listing among the factors.

I'm weighing whether the revert was judged too quickly, since flag-on evaluations and ZeroDivisionErrors kept showing up after it was logged. The verdict that the mitigation failed rested on that, and the incident document already calls for confirming that a change actually reached the service.

I'm now checking whether the revert actually reached every evaluation, since flag-on evaluations and ZeroDivisionErrors still show up in the minutes after the switch-off. The question is whether the change propagated to every replica, and whether those later errors came only from flag-on requests.

Writing the remaining root-cause and plain-language summary items now...

Working out the action items now: the first is to require the code path behind a feature flag to be exercised by tests before the flag can be switched on.

Checking the action items now: one is to require the code path behind a feature flag to be exercised by tests before the flag is switched on in production, and another is to route the sustained error-rate alert on the shop service to page on-call.

Next I'm noting which went-well points are actually supported: the investigator placed the onset and tied it to the admin's flag change, the mitigation agent reverted the flag and that revert is reversible, and the code-fix agent proposed a draft fix. I'll name those three without describing what the fix does, and I'm not adding anything to the got-lucky list since the record doesn't show a lucky break.

I'm reviewing what went wrong: the revert was judged to have failed even though flag-on evaluations and errors still showed up after it, and the flag was put back on. I'm also noting that the account page requests were what carried the failures in the first place.

Checking the flag-on evaluations: the first one shows up at 22:25, and the switch-on is logged at 22:24, so I'm lining up those timestamps against the flag change and the error logs.

Writing the assumptions section now: the account page errors are attributed to shoppers with past purchases but none this month, based on Code-Fix's reading rather than a log line, and the flag's on and off states are being read as per-request evaluations from the logs.

action_items.item: Require tests to run the code path behind a feature flag on io-shop, with the flag on, before that flag can be switched on in production.
Route the ErrorRateSustained alert on io-shop to page the on-call person.
Find out what delayed ErrorRateSustained by {beyond_accounted_for} beyond what its evaluation and scraping account for, and remove that delay.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed far more often than usual.
The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47.

ruled_out.what: A deploy: none came back among the production changes read. As of {T32.1}, all replicas ran one revision.

causal_chain.step: Account page requests started running the code path that holds that division because admin switched the feature flag monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}. Requests evaluating the flag as on appear from the onset minute on, and the ZeroDivisionErrors fall in the same minutes as those on evaluations.
On that path, the monthly average spend per item divides this month's total by the number of this month's purchases, and that number is zero for a shopper who has bought before but not this month.

input.cause_in_plain_words: An administrator switched on a setting that sent shoppers' account pages through a calculation that divides by zero, likely for shoppers who had bought before but not this month.

contributing_factors.factor: Before monthly-spend-feature was switched on in production, no check was seen that ran the code path behind it, including for shoppers with past purchases but none this month.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The division by zero on the flag-on path would have been caught before the flag reached shoppers, so their account pages would not have failed.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The ErrorRateSustained alert on io-shop paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A person would have been brought in while account pages were still failing and could have acted alongside Argus, which might have shortened the incident.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: The alert fired {beyond_accounted_for} later than its evaluation interval and scraping allowance account for, and the record does not show what took the extra time.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The alert, and the response that followed it, would have come sooner after the onset.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent tied the onset to admin switching monthly-spend-feature on and named the ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 as the failure.
The Mitigation Agent reverted monthly-spend-feature with an action that could be put back.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as draft pull request #424 for a person to review.

went_wrong: After monthly-spend-feature was switched off at the provider, account page requests in some minutes still evaluated it as on, and the ZeroDivisionErrors fell in those same minutes. Even so, the revert was judged as not helping and the flag was switched back on.

input.root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, the account page computes `average_spend_per_item_this_month` as `account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought_this_month)`, where `bought_this_month` is the account's purchases filtered to `in_current_month`. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month that list is empty, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 and the account page request fails.
input.still_at_risk: With monthly-spend-feature back on, account page requests could keep failing with the division-by-zero error.
input.stops_the_harm: Switch monthly-spend-feature off again. At io-shop, confirm that account page requests log only monthly-spend-feature=off evaluations, with no monthly-spend-feature=on lines, and that the ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 stops appearing.
input.symptom: Shoppers' account pages failed to load
input.why_it_did_not_help: Find out why account page requests still evaluated monthly-spend-feature as on in some minutes after it was switched off at the flag provider: check whether the off setting reached every replica and every evaluation, and whether the ZeroDivisionErrors after the revert came only from requests that evaluated the flag as on.
